why_next: The V1_BUFFERED_PROXY_NOT_STREAMING blocker is resolved at the HTTP Transfer-Encoding framing layer: the streaming proxy forwards partial chunks without full-body buffering and the decompressor processes the accumulated bytes with byte-identical output to buffered ground truth across all 840 observations (480 multi-layer + 240 regression + 120 identity). However, localhost correctness does not imply CDN correctness. Real CDNs (Cloudflare, Fastly, Akamai) introduce Accept-Encoding negotiation, Vary/cache headers, geographic latency, TCP segmentation, concurrent clients, and potentially different chunked TE framing behavior — none of which are tested on localhost. The CDN correctness gate is the sole remaining blocker for C-MEAS-VALID Product Core readiness. A positive result would close the full decompression-correctness chain (single-layer → multi-layer → streaming framing → CDN); a negative result would identify CDN-specific decompression failures requiring diagnosis. This is materially orthogonal to the localhost framing test just completed and cannot be inferred from it.

recommended_action: Design and execute a real CDN decompression correctness experiment using Cloudflare or Fastly free tier: serve high-entropy multi-layer compressed payloads through a real CDN with Accept-Encoding negotiation, auth-aware Vary/cache, and measure whether iterative decompression (brotli->gzip->identity, max_depth=5) produces byte-identical output to ground-truth at 8KB+ chunk sizes. The localhost framing-layer validation (this experiment) and multi-layer validation (EXP-RUNTIME-35513777099) establish the baseline; CDN infrastructure introduces Accept-Encoding negotiation, Vary/cache, geographic latency, TCP segmentation, and concurrent clients that cannot be replicated on localhost. If CDN passes, C-MEAS-VALID is ready for Product Core promotion. If CDN fails, diagnose whether the failure is in Accept-Encoding negotiation, cache/Vary semantics, geographic chunking, or decompression under CDN-specific response structures. Optionally, test true incremental decompressor APIs (brotli.Decompressor.process / gzip streaming without accumulation) as a parallel investigation — the present test proves Transfer-Encoding framing is safe but does not test the decompressor streaming API layer.
